title: The pause, and "Arise and warn"
hook: After the first revelation, silence. Then the angel appeared again.

screens.text: **After the first revelation, silence.** No angel. No new verses. Then one day, out walking, he heard a voice, looked up, and saw the angel of Hira again.

**A quiet stretch.** After the first verses, revelation paused for a while. Then, as he walked, he saw the same angel from Hira, between the sky and the earth. Frightened, he went home and asked to be wrapped up [Bukhari 4].
bubbles: How long the pause lasted isn't certain. Reports range from days to much longer, so we just say "a while" [Qalam ep. 29].

options.feedback: Yes. The quiet was over. Now he was told to stand up and call people to Allah.
Not quite. The verse says "Arise and warn". The pause was ending, and the work was beginning.
Not quite. He was told to arise and warn, not to stay wrapped up.

screens.text: **Get up.** Allah revealed the opening of the **surah** al-Muddaththir ("the one wrapped up"): arise, warn, and glorify your Lord [Q 74:1–5]. After that, revelation kept coming, steadily and often [Bukhari 4; IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: The silence wasn't the end. It turned out to be a pause before the real work began.

events.title: The first verses
events.text: In the cave of Hira, the opening of Surah al-'Alaq [Bukhari 3].

events.title: The angel again
events.text: Between the sky and the earth. He goes home and asks to be wrapped up [Bukhari 4].

events.title: Arise and warn
events.text: The opening of Surah al-Muddaththir comes down. Revelation now comes steadily [Q 74:1–5; Bukhari 4].

events.title: Not abandoned
events.text: Ill for a few nights, he's mocked. Surah al-Duha answers [Bukhari 4950].

screens.text: **"Your Lord has not left you."** Once, ill, he missed his night prayer for a few nights. A woman mocked that his "devil" had left him. Allah answered: *"Your Lord has not taken leave of you, [O Muhammad], nor has He detested [you]"* [Q 93:3, Saheeh Intl.].
bubbles: That was a different occasion from the first pause [Bukhari 4950].

screens.text: Drag along the line. A dip isn't the end of the story.

points.label: It all feels new
points.text: The first weeks after your shahada can feel bright and close.

points.label: A quiet stretch
points.text: Prayers feel flat. Allah feels far. Feeling low is not leaving Islam.

points.label: Still showing up
points.text: All five prayers are still due. Pray each one with what you've got, even when it feels dry.

points.label: Closeness returns
points.text: Like revelation after the pause, it comes back, often stronger than before.

screens.text: **Quiet isn't goodbye.** Even the Prophet ﷺ went through a silence, and was mocked for it. If your **iman** (faith) has dipped and your prayers feel empty, it doesn't mean Allah has left you. Keep showing up.

screens.situation: Dre took his shahada four months ago. The first weeks felt electric. Now prayer feels like a chore, and he wonders if he was ever really Muslim.

options.text: Keep praying with what he has, tell his mentor how he feels, and remember even the Prophet ﷺ had quiet stretches
options.feedback: Yes. Dry spells are normal. Showing up through them is how faith grows back.

options.text: Decide the feeling proves his Islam wasn't real
options.feedback: Not quite. Feeling low is not leaving Islam. Leaving is a choice to reject it.

options.text: Stop praying until the feeling comes back
options.feedback: Not quite. All five are still due. Praying through the dry spell is what brings the closeness back.

screens.text: The silence wasn't Allah leaving him, and a dry spell isn't Allah leaving you.
Next episode: the first people to believe him: his wife, his best friend, a boy and a freed man.

check.prompt: What did Allah reveal after the pause?

options.text: The opening of Surah al-Muddaththir: arise and warn
options.feedback: Right. After that, revelation came steadily [Q 74:1–5; Bukhari 4].
Not quite. It came bit by bit over many years. After the pause came "Arise and warn" [Q 74:1–5].

check.prompt: What's the lesson of the pause for a new Muslim?

options.text: A quiet spell in your faith doesn't mean Allah has left you
options.feedback: Right. Keep showing up; closeness comes back.

options.text: If faith feels flat, you were never really Muslim
options.feedback: Not quite. Feeling low is not leaving Islam. Even the Prophet ﷺ went through a silence.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- After the first revelation there was a pause. Then, walking, he saw the angel of Hira between the sky and the earth, went home frightened and asked to be wrapped up [Bukhari 4]. Bukhari 3 also mentions the pause after Waraqah's death.
- Allah revealed Q 74:1–5 (arise and warn; glorify your Lord); after that, revelation came steadily [Bukhari 4; IslamQA 11575].
- The pause's length is disputed (from days to much longer) [Qalam ep. 29]; say "a while".
- Another time, when he was ill and missed his night prayer for two or three nights, a woman taunted that his "devil" had left him; Surah al-Duha was revealed: your Lord has not left you, nor does He hate you [Bukhari 4950; Q 93:1–3]. This was a separate occasion; don't merge it with the first pause.

**Likely questions**
- *"Is it true he thought of throwing himself off a mountain during the pause?"* Explain briefly and calmly: that report is not authentic. It's an unconnected addition by a later narrator (al-Zuhri) to one version in al-Bukhari's collection, not part of the hadith's chain, and scholars don't accept it [IslamQA 152611]. Don't repeat the details. (scholar question Q43)
- *"Why did revelation pause?"* The texts don't give a reason. Some scholars reflect that it let him settle and long for more; present that as reflection, not fact.
- *"My iman feels low. Is that normal?"* Yes. Feeling low is not leaving Islam; leaving is a choice to reject it (scholar question Q20). All five prayers stay due; pray each with what you have (scholar question Q4). Point to Day 12, Day 25 and Day 45.
- *"What does Surah al-Duha say?"* Your Lord hasn't left you or hated you [Q 93:1–3]; the surah goes on to remind him how Allah sheltered him as an orphan (seerah-04, Q 93:6–8).

**Escalate:** if a convert mentions hopelessness, self-harm or suicide, stop teaching and follow the safety rule (988 and the other crisis resources; offer to alert someone they choose). Never only the imam queue.

**Don't**
- Don't tell or hint at the mountain report as fact.
- Don't link Bukhari 4950 to the first pause.
- Don't treat a dip in iman as a sin or as apostasy.
- Don't describe the angel's appearance beyond the hadith, and don't picture him.
